arxiv-2008-01307.title: The Jazz Transformer on the Front Line: Exploring the Shortcomings of AI-composed Music through Quantitative Measures
arxiv-2008-01307.description: Abstract This paper presents the Jazz Transformer, a generative model that utilizes a neural sequence model called the Transformer-XL for modeling lead sheets of Jazz music. Moreover, the model endeavors to incorporate structural events present in the Weimar Jazz Database (WJazzD) for inducing structures in the generated music.

arxiv-2104-08176.creator: Lech Pasicki
arxiv-2104-08176.description: Abstract The manuscript contains elegant extensions of the fundamental variational principles: Brøndsted’s and Ekeland’s. On the other hand, we get general and precise version of the Takahashi and the Caristi fixed point theorems. The results are based on the notion of istance for uniform spaces. The main results of this paper are theorems of variational type for uniform spaces.

arxiv-2206-08238.title: Topological insulators in semiclassical regime
arxiv-2206-08238.creator: Alexis Drouot
arxiv-2206-08238.description: Abstract Abstract. We study solutions of 2\times 2 systems (hD_{t}+\not{D})\Psi_{t}=0 on \mathbb{R}^{2} in the semiclassical regime h\rightarrow 0 . Our Dirac operator \not{D} is a standard model for interfaces between topological insulators: it represents a semimetal at null energy, and distinct topological phases at positive / negative energies.

arxiv-2310-01145.title: Parallel-in-Time Probabilistic Numerical ODE Solvers
arxiv-2310-01145.creator: Nathanael Bosch nathanael.bosch@uni-tuebingen.de, Adrien Corenflos adrien.corenflos.stats@gmail.com, Fatemeh Yaghoobi fatemeh.yaghoobi@aalto.fi, Filip Tronarp filip.tronarp@matstat.lu.se, Philipp Hennig philipp.hennig@uni-tuebingen.de, Simo Särkkä simo.sarkka@aalto.fi
arxiv-2310-01145.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nathanael Bosch nathanael.bosch@uni-tuebingen.de, Adrien Corenflos adrien.corenflos.stats@gmail.com, Fatemeh Yaghoobi fatemeh.yaghoobi@aalto.fi, Filip Tronarp filip.tronarp@matstat.lu.se, Philipp Hennig philipp.hennig@uni-tuebingen.de, Simo Särkkä simo.sarkka@aalto.fi. Probabilistic numerical solvers for ordinary differential equations (ODEs) treat the numerical simulation of dynamical systems as problems of Bayesian state estimation. Aside from producing posterior distributions over ODE solutions and thereby quantifying the numerical approximation error of the method itself, one less-often noted advantage of this formalism is the algorithmic flexibility gained by formulating numerical simulation in the framework of Bayesian filtering and smoothing.

arxiv-2504-18483.description: Abstract The ability to generate explanations that are understood by explainees is the quintessence of explainable artificial intelligence.
